# context.capability.47: one line per command that takes an id, spelled as canon 0.30 took it (`--<noun>-id`).
# `cli_ids.rs` runs each line in order on one fresh repo, with the bare spelling, and compares the exit, the output and
# the stored records with what canon 0.30 printed and wrote for the 0.30 spelling (`expected.txt`). A line starting
# with `git` runs git, one starting with `rm` removes a file. The fixture holds no brief: the brief format is another
# change of 0.31. Bless with a 0.30 binary: `CANON_030_BIN=<path> cargo test -p canon-cli --test cli_ids context_capability_47`.
subject new demo --domain dev --title Demo --actor-id planner-1 --session-id s-1 --json
change new add-login --subject-id demo --title "Add login" --json
rm .canon/changes/add-login/brief.md
subject unadopt demo --change-id add-login --json
subject adopt demo --change-id add-login --json
subject unadopt demo --change-id add-login --json
retrieve --for-role reviewer --domain dev --subject-id demo --json
scenario new demo.login.01 --title "Signs in" --subject-id demo --case happy --actor-id planner-1 --session-id s-1 --project-id root --json
feature new demo.signup --title Signup --actor-id planner-1 --session-id s-1 --project-id root --json
rm .canon/specs/kind=feature/area=demo/signup.feature
git add -A
git commit -q -m specs
inventory sync --json
evidence add --scenario-id demo.login.01 --project-id root --class test-run --ref "npm test" --role implementer --actor-id impl-1 --session-id s-2 --json

finding close add-login --round 1 --seq 1 --disposition rejected --reason "accepted" --actor-id impl-1 --session-id s-2 --json
gate promote --json

query --kind evidence --plugin-id none --json
